name: Millstone
overview: The topic of the millstone in Scripture carries significant weight both literally and figuratively. It is forbidden to be taken as a pledge because it represents a person's life, emphasizing its preciousness (Deuteronomy 24:6). The millstone is also associated with severe judgment, as illustrated by the warnings in the Gospels that it is better to be drowned with a millstone hung around the neck than to cause harm to believers (Matthew 18:6; Mark 9:42; Luke 17:2). Additionally, millstones were likely used in executions by drowning, and the story of Abimelech's death by a millstone striking his head shows its deadly physical power (Judges 9:53). Figuratively, the hardness of a millstone is used to describe a stubborn, hard heart (Job 41:24), underscoring the spiritual seriousness of resistance to God's will.
